# This file lives in .github/workflows/ in your repo. GitHub reads every
# YAML file in that folder and runs it as an automated "workflow".
#
# What this workflow does, in plain words:
#   1. Builds your React app into static files (HTML, CSS, JS).
#   2. Publishes those files to GitHub Pages so they're live on the internet.

# The name shown in the "Actions" tab of your repo. It's just a label.
name: Deploy

# TRIGGER: when should this workflow run?
on:
  push:                # run whenever someone pushes commits...
    branches:
      - master         # ...to the master branch (and only that branch)

# PERMISSIONS (default for every job in this file)
# Every job gets a temporary password called GITHUB_TOKEN. It lets the job
# talk to GitHub (read code, create deployments, etc.). This block decides
# what that token is allowed to do. Anything not listed is switched off.
permissions:
  contents: read       # read your repo's files (needed to check out the code)
  pages: write         # create a GitHub Pages deployment
  id-token: write      # let the job prove its identity to GitHub (see "deploy" job)

# A workflow is made of jobs. Each job runs on its own brand-new virtual
# machine, so jobs do NOT share files with each other unless you pass
# them explicitly (we do that below with an "artifact").
jobs:

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # JOB 1: build. Turns your source code into the files to publish.
  # This job inherits the top-level permissions above.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest      # the type of virtual machine to use

    # Steps run one after another, top to bottom, on that machine.
    steps:

      # The machine starts empty. This copies your repo's code onto it.
      # (This is the step that needs "contents: read".)
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v6   # "uses" = run a ready-made action

      # Installs Node.js so npm commands work.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:                       # "with" = settings passed to the action
          node-version: 20
          cache: npm                # reuse downloaded packages between runs (faster)

      # Installs the exact package versions listed in package-lock.json.
      # Stricter and more repeatable than "npm install".
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci                 # "run" = type this command in a terminal

      # Compiles your React app. The output goes into the ./build folder.
      - name: Build React app
        run: npm run build

      # Asks GitHub about your Pages settings (site URL, base path) and checks
      # that Pages is switched on for this repo. It makes those values
      # available to later steps, but nothing in this file uses them, and it
      # runs after the build is already done. So for this React app it is
      # effectively just a safety check, and you could delete it.
      - name: Configure GitHub Pages
        uses: actions/configure-pages@v5

      # Packs the ./build folder into a single compressed file (a "tarball")
      # and stores it with this workflow run as an ARTIFACT.
      # - "path" is the only thing we choose: which folder to pack.
      # - The artifact's name is NOT written here. It defaults to
      #   "github-pages" inside the action itself.
      # - Nothing is published yet. The live site hasn't changed.
      # This is how files get from the build machine to the deploy machine.
      - name: Upload build artifact
        uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: ./build             # use ./dist instead if you use Vite

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # JOB 2: deploy. Takes the packed files and publishes them.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  deploy:
    needs: build                    # wait for "build" to succeed first.
                                    # This only controls ORDER. It does not
                                    # copy files between jobs.

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest          # a second, separate fresh machine

    # A job-level "permissions" block REPLACES the top-level one for this job
    # (it does not add to it). So this job gets only these two permissions
    # and loses "contents: read", which is fine because it never checks out
    # code. That's why permissions appear twice: top-level is the default,
    # and this job narrows it down to what it needs.
    permissions:
      pages: write      # allowed to create the Pages deployment
      id-token: write   # allowed to request an OIDC token: a signed proof of
                        # "this request really comes from this repo's workflow".
                        # The deploy action sends it to GitHub Pages.

    # ENVIRONMENT: connects this job to a GitHub "Environment" named
    # github-pages. Pages deployments must be linked to one. It gives you
    # the "Deployments" history in your repo sidebar, and it's where rules
    # such as "only master may deploy" or "needs a reviewer's approval" live.
    # (This is a different thing from the artifact, which just happens to
    # share the same name.)
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      # Puts a clickable link to the live site on the deployment. The value
      # comes from the step below, found through its id ("deployment").
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}

    steps:
      # Finds the artifact called "github-pages" from this same workflow run
      # (its default name matches the upload step's default), downloads it,
      # and tells GitHub Pages to publish it. The live site changes here.
      # The "id" lets other parts of the file read this step's outputs,
      # such as page_url above.
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        id: deployment
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
